transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to see me?

Well, I came in because... honestly, my husband and the people at the warehouse keep acting like I'm crazy. But I know what's going on. I know they've been watching my every move at work. They keep changing the pallet counts on my shifts just to mess with me, to keep me from getting that supervisor spot.
How long have you been noticing that people at work are watching you and changing the pallet counts?

It's been about eight months now. That's when I really started noticing them watching me and messing with the things at work. And, well, the voices, too... all of that has been happening for about eight months.
When you hear these voices, what do they say to you? Do they give you commands or instructions, or do they comment on what you're doing?

It's mostly just this one man's voice. He tells me to do things... like an instruction, I guess. Sometimes when I'm in the aisle at work, or even just at home folding clothes, I'll hear him clear as day. He tells me, Nicole, check it again. And I always look around, but there's never anybody anywhere near me.

Over these eight months when you've been hearing the voice and noticing people watching you, have there been times when you felt unusually energetic, needed very little sleep, or had racing thoughts? Or have there been periods where you felt very depressed or hopeless?

Yeah, there were times like that. Like, for a few weeks, I was barely sleeping at all, but I felt like I could just keep going. I was pushing extra shifts at work, doing boxing, and helping out with a bunch of church work. 

But the thing is... even during those weeks when I was doing all that and not really sleeping, I was also hearing that man's voice. And I was still feeling sure that the people at the warehouse were setting me up.

When you were having those weeks with very little sleep and lots of energy, were the voices and the feeling that people were watching you happening the whole time during those weeks, or did they come and go?

They were happening the whole time, yeah. But... it wasn't just during those energetic times. Even during a quieter few weeks, like when I was sleeping closer to normal and not racing around so much, I still heard the voice telling me to check things. And I still knew for a fact they were changing the pallet counts against me. It doesn't really stop just because I'm sleeping better or slowing down.

When you were having those weeks with lots of energy and barely sleeping, did the voice telling you to check things and the feeling that people were watching you seem to match up with how you were feeling—like they made sense with your mood at the time? Or did they feel separate from your mood, like they were happening regardless of how you felt?

I'm not really sure what you mean by matching up, but... I guess they feel separate. Like I was saying, they just happen regardless of how I'm feeling. 

Whether I'm super energized and moving fast, or just having a regular, quiet day, the voice is still there telling me to check things. And I still know they're messing with my pallets at the warehouse. It doesn't really change based on my mood or my energy... it's just happening anyway.

When you were in those weeks feeling super energetic and not sleeping much, did the voice telling you to check things and the belief that people were sabotaging you feel like they fit with that excited, energized mood—like they made sense as part of feeling that way? Or did they feel completely separate from your mood?

I mean, like I was just saying... they really just feel separate. I don't fully get what you mean by them fitting with my mood, to be honest. 

It's not like the voice gets all hyped up just because I've got a lot of energy. It's just the same voice. And the guys at the warehouse, that situation is just happening no matter what. It doesn't change if I'm excited or if I'm tired. So yeah, definitely separate. I don't really know how else to explain it.

Have there been times in these eight months when you felt completely normal—not energized, not depressed, just regular—and during those times, did the voice and the feeling that people were watching you go away completely?

Like I mentioned earlier, no, they don't go away. Even when I have a few weeks where things are pretty quiet, you know, when I'm sleeping normal and not rushing around, the voice is still there. It's still telling me to check things. And I still know they're messing with the pallet counts against me. So, even when I feel regular, those things are still happening.

During those quiet weeks when you're sleeping normally and feeling just regular—not excited, not depressed—have there been any days or stretches of time when the voice completely stopped and you didn't feel like people were watching you or messing with the pallets?

No, they never completely stop. Like I just said, even during those quieter weeks when I'm sleeping closer to normal and I'm not racing around so much, I still hear the voice telling me to check things. And I still know they're changing the pallet counts against me. It doesn't just go away.
